name: Active Reload
text: While reloading, pressing Reload during the highlighted portion will instantly finish your reload and grant you Fire Rate, Bullet Lifesteal and Move Speed.

effects.text: While reloading, pressing Reload during the highlighted portion will instantly finish your reload and grant you Fire Rate, Bullet Lifesteal and Move Speed.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 weapon item that costs 1,600 souls. It adds 20% to your magazine size all the time. It also adds a timing game to reloading: press Reload during the highlighted part of the reload and it finishes at once.
beginner.whyItMatters: A well-timed reload gives you +25% fire rate, +16% bullet lifesteal and +0.75 m/s move speed for 7 seconds. It can only trigger once every 12 seconds, so it rewards a clean press, not mashing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it when you shoot a lot and are comfortable watching your reload bar. Try to time the press every time the 12 second cooldown is up, because the bonus is worth the attention.

name: Alchemical Fire
text: Throw a flask that explodes on contact, creating an area that does increasing spirit damage per second and reduces enemy Bullet Resist. 50% less effective vs non-heroes.

effects.text: Throw a flask that explodes on contact, creating an area that does increasing spirit damage per second and reduces enemy Bullet Resist. 50% less effective vs non-heroes.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 weapon item with a button. Press it to throw a flask that bursts on contact and leaves a burning patch with a 10 metre radius for 5 seconds. Enemies standing in it take damage over time (45 per second at the start, rising to 95) and lose 7% Bullet Resist. It also adds 10 Spirit Power.
beginner.whyItMatters: Lowering Bullet Resist makes every bullet from you and your teammates hit harder against anyone in the fire, so it is both a damage tool and a setup tool. The effect is 50% weaker against troopers and other non-player targets.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it when your team trades lots of bullets and you fight over a fixed spot such as a doorway or an objective. Throw it where enemies have to stand, then shoot into it. The cooldown is 30 seconds.

name: Arcane Surge
text: After you Dash-Jump, the next ability you use within 7s will have bonus Range, Duration, and Spirit Power.

effects.text: After you Dash-Jump, the next ability you use within 7s will have bonus Range, Duration, and Spirit Power.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 spirit item that costs 1,600 souls and is built from Extra Stamina. After you dash-jump, the next ability you use within 7 seconds gets 12% more range, 15% more duration and 20 Spirit Power. It also adds 1 Stamina and 12% Stamina recovery.
beginner.whyItMatters: It links movement to power: a dash before a spell makes the spell stronger. The bonus only appears if you cast within the 7 second window.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it for a mobile ability hero who moves before casting. If you cast from a standing position, you will not trigger it.

name: Arctic Blast
text: Release an expanding ice blast that deals spirit damage, Freezing and then Slowing targets it hits. Slowed targets have their stamina regen frozen

effects.text: Release an expanding ice blast that deals spirit damage, Freezing and then Slowing targets it hits. Slowed targets have their stamina regen frozen

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 spirit item with a button, built from Cold Front. Press it to release an expanding ice blast out to a radius of 16 metres that deals 175 damage, freezes enemies for 1 second and then slows them. Slowed targets cannot recover Stamina. The cooldown is 24 seconds. It also adds 10% resistance to spirit damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: A freeze followed by a slow gives your team a reliable chance to catch and kill a group.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it when enemies are close together and you want to lock them down for your team to finish. Buy it after Cold Front.

name: Armor Piercer
text: Your Bullets have a chance to become unavoidable, piercing through enemies and ignoring their Bullet Resistance.

effects.text: Your Bullets have a chance to become unavoidable, piercing through enemies and ignoring their Bullet Resistance.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 weapon item that costs 6,400 souls and is built from High-Velocity Rounds. It adds 60% bullet speed and 8% Weapon Damage. More than half of your shots (55%) turn into special bullets that nothing can block: they go straight through the enemies in their path and their Bullet Resist does not count.
beginner.whyItMatters: Ignoring Bullet Resist matters most against enemies who stacked a lot of it, because their defence simply does not apply to the bullets that trigger the effect. Faster bullets are also easier to land on moving targets.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it late in the game when enemy tanks are shrugging off your bullets. It is a poor pick if the other team has built almost no Bullet Resist.

name: Ballistic Enchantment
text: Imbue an ability with increased range. Dealing damage with that ability grants you increased weapon damage per unique hero hit. Has reduced effect on non-heroes.

effects.text: Imbue an ability with increased range. Dealing damage with that ability grants you increased weapon damage per unique hero hit. Has reduced effect on non-heroes.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 weapon item that costs 3,200 souls and is built from Mystic Expansion. You attach it to one of your abilities, which then reaches 22% farther. When that ability damages a hero you gain 20% Weapon Damage for each different hero hit, for 20 seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns an ability into a way to power up your gun. Hitting several heroes with one cast stacks the bonus higher, and the bonus is smaller (5% each, up to 8 stacks) when the ability only hits troopers or other non-player targets.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pick it for a hero whose favourite ability hits an area or lands often, and who also spends time shooting. It does little for a hero who never fires a weapon.

name: Battle Vest
text: While you are above 65% health, gain weapon damage and bonus fire rate.

effects.text: While you are above 65% health, gain weapon damage and bonus fire rate.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 vitality item that costs 1,600 souls. It always gives 18% Bullet Resist and 3 extra regeneration out of combat. On top of that, while you are above 65% health you gain 18% Weapon Damage and 7% fire rate.
beginner.whyItMatters: The defence is always on, but the offence needs you healthy: once you drop to 65% health or below, the damage and fire rate bonus switches off.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A solid choice for a hero who starts fights at full health and has ways to avoid damage. If you often fight from low health you keep the Bullet Resist but lose the damage.

name: Berserker
text: Your Weapon Damage increases as you take sustained damage.

effects.text: Your Weapon Damage increases as you take sustained damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 weapon item that costs 3,200 souls. Every time you take 120 damage you gain a stack worth 7% Weapon Damage, up to 10 stacks, and a stack lasts 10 seconds. It also gives 8% Bullet Resist.
beginner.whyItMatters: The more punishment you absorb, the harder you shoot back. Each stack adds 7% Weapon Damage, up to 10 stacks, which turns a long brawl into your advantage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it for a hero who fights up close and takes a lot of hits. It needs you to survive the damage, so pair it with health or healing, and skip it if you usually fight from far away.

name: Blood Tribute
text: Toggle: Continually sacrifice Health to improve fire rate, Debuff Resistance and Move Speed.

effects.text: Toggle: Continually sacrifice Health to improve fire rate, Debuff Resistance and Move Speed.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 weapon item you switch on and off. While it is on you lose 50 health per second and gain 35% fire rate, 35% Debuff Resist and 2 metres per second of move speed. It also gives 8% Debuff Resist, 8% Spirit Resist and 4 extra regeneration out of combat.
beginner.whyItMatters: You are paying health for speed and damage, so it is strongest when you can win a fight in a few seconds. Leaving it on by accident drains you fast.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Switch it on when you commit to a fight you expect to win quickly or when you need to chase, and switch it off the moment the fight is over. Do not buy it if your hero has no way to heal.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 spirit item that costs 6,400 souls and is built from Improved Spirit. It adds 30 Spirit Power and raises your Spirit Power by 15%. It also adds 75 health and 4 extra regeneration out of combat. It has no button.
beginner.whyItMatters: Everything that scales with Spirit Power gets stronger: ability damage, healing and shields. The 15% multiplier grows more valuable the more Spirit Power you already own.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it late for a hero who wins fights with abilities, and complete the line from Extra Spirit and Improved Spirit first.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 vitality item that costs 1,600 souls. 13% of the weapon damage you deal comes back to you as health. It also adds 90 health and 6% Weapon Damage. It builds into Fury Trance, Leech and Vampiric Burst.
beginner.whyItMatters: Every bullet that lands also heals you, so the more you shoot, the longer you survive. This is one of the main ways to stay in a fight without a healer.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it for a hero who shoots constantly. If your damage mostly comes from abilities, Spirit Lifesteal is the better match.

name: Bullet Resilience
text: When below 50% health, gain additional Bullet Resist.

effects.text: When below 50% health, gain additional Bullet Resist.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 vitality item that costs 3,200 souls. It gives 30% Bullet Resist, plus another 15% when you are below 50% health. It also adds 3 extra regeneration out of combat.
beginner.whyItMatters: The extra defence arrives just when you are in trouble, which makes it hard to finish off a hurt player who is being shot.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it when the enemy team does most of its damage with bullets. If they rely on abilities, pick Spirit Resilience instead.

name: Bullet Resist Shredder
text: Reduces Bullet Resist on enemies when you deal spirit damage.

effects.text: Reduces Bullet Resist on enemies when you deal spirit damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 spirit item that costs 1,600 souls. Dealing spirit damage lowers the target's Bullet Resist by 10% for 8 seconds. It also adds 9% Bullet Resist and 9% Weapon Damage for you.
beginner.whyItMatters: Your ability damage makes your team's bullets hit harder. It is a good bridge for a hero who mixes abilities and weapon damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it when your team relies on bullets and you have abilities that land often.

name: Burst Fire
text: Briefly gain Fire Rate and Move Speed when one of your bullets hits a hero.

effects.text: Briefly gain Fire Rate and Move Speed when one of your bullets hits a hero.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 weapon item that costs 3,200 souls and is built from Rapid Rounds. When one of your bullets hits a hero you gain 32% fire rate and 1.25 metres per second of move speed for 4.5 seconds. It can trigger once every 9 seconds. It also adds 10% fire rate all the time.
beginner.whyItMatters: The bonus starts the moment you land a shot, so it rewards opening a fight with a hit. The 9 second cooldown means it does not stay on forever.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A good fit for a hero who fires steadily and wants a burst of speed to start a fight or to escape after the first hit. Open with a sure shot to trigger it.

name: Capacitor
text: Your bullets have a chance to shock your target. The shock will jump to a nearby enemy. Launch a projectile that deals damage, applies a strong slow that recovers over time, prevents Stamina usage and Silences their movement-based items and abilities.

effects.text: Your bullets have a chance to shock your target. The shock will jump to a nearby enemy.
Launch a projectile that deals damage, applies a strong slow that recovers over time, prevents Stamina usage and Silences their movement-based items and abilities.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 weapon item with a button, built from Tesla Bullets. Your bullets have a 20% chance to shock a target, and the shock jumps to as many as 6 other enemies within 10 metres. Press the button to launch a projectile that deals 100 damage, heavily slows the target and stops them from using Stamina or movement items. It also adds 5% fire rate.
beginner.whyItMatters: The passive spreads damage across a group, and the button can catch an enemy who is trying to run. Cutting off Stamina and movement items makes it hard to escape.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it as an upgrade to Tesla Bullets when you want to pick off fleeing enemies and fight groups. The cooldown is 40 seconds, so aim the button at the target you most want to catch.

name: Celestial Blessing
text: Applies an extremely powerful cleanse that replenishes your allies globally.

effects.text: Applies an extremely powerful cleanse that replenishes your allies globally.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 5 Street Brawl legendary with a button; it only exists in that mode and is never sold, but it can turn up in the item draft. Press it to cleanse and heal your allies everywhere on the map, giving +100% stamina recovery and +5 m/s move speed for 6 seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: Its heal is listed as 60% with a minimum of 400, and it reaches teammates who are far away, so it can save a whole team after a bad fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only in Street Brawl. Press it when your team has taken a lot of damage together, not when only one person is hurt.

name: Cheat Death
text: When you would take lethal damage, instead become temporarily death immune and remove all non-stun debuffs. While death immune, you deal reduced damage and have reduced healing.

effects.text: When you would take lethal damage, instead become temporarily death immune and remove all non-stun debuffs. While death immune, you deal reduced damage and have reduced healing.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 vitality item that costs 6,400 souls. When you would take lethal damage you survive instead, become immune to death for 4.5 seconds and lose all negative effects except stuns. During that time you deal 60% less damage and receive 60% less healing. The cooldown is 90 seconds. It also adds 200 health and 15% Bullet Resist.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives you one extra life per fight, and you have 4.5 seconds to run away, finish a kill or get healed. It cannot trigger again until the 90 seconds are over.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A good choice for carries and any hero who will be focused first. Plan an escape or a finishing move the moment it triggers.

name: Cloak of Opportunity
text: Block the next debuff that would apply movement lock, Stun, Chained, Immobilize, or Sleep and become Unstoppable. Also gain a Barrier and bonus move speed

effects.text: Block the next debuff that would apply movement lock, Stun, Chained, Immobilize, or Sleep and become Unstoppable. Also gain a Barrier and bonus move speed

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 5 vitality legendary from the Street Brawl mode, picked in the item draft rather than bought. It blocks the next stun, chain, immobilise, sleep or movement lock, makes you unstoppable for 4 seconds, and gives you a 500 point Barrier and 3 metres per second of move speed for 6 seconds. The cooldown is 12 seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It protects you from stuns, slows and other effects that would otherwise take you out of the fight, and it comes back quickly.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only used in Street Brawl. Take it when enemy heroes keep trying to lock you down.

name: Close Quarters
text: Deal additional Weapon Damage when in close range to your target.

effects.text: Deal additional Weapon Damage when in close range to your target.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 1 weapon item that costs 800 souls. It gives +20% weapon damage against targets within 15m and 20% Melee Resist. It has no button.
beginner.whyItMatters: It strongly favors fighting close to enemies, and the melee resist helps when a brawler is next to you. It builds into Point-Blank.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it on a hero who fights up close, such as a brawler or a shotgun user. It does less for a sniper who stays far away.

name: Cold Front
text: Release an expanding ice blast that deals spirit damage and Slows targets it hits.

effects.text: Release an expanding ice blast that deals spirit damage and Slows targets it hits.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 spirit item with a button that costs 1,600 souls. Press it to release an expanding ice blast out to a radius of 10 metres that deals 95 damage and slows enemies by 48% for 4 seconds. The cooldown is 25 seconds. It also adds 6% resistance to spirit damage. It builds into Arctic Blast.
beginner.whyItMatters: A reliable slow lets you chase or run away. It is also the first step toward Arctic Blast.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it to stop a fleeing enemy or when a group rushes you. Keep it ready for the moment fights begin.

name: Colossus
text: Grow larger in size, gaining bullet resist, spirit resist, and melee damage. Nearby enemies suffer from slow and have reduced dash speed.

effects.text: Grow larger in size, gaining bullet resist, spirit resist, and melee damage. Nearby enemies suffer from slow and have reduced dash speed.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 vitality item with a button, built from Extra Health. Press it to grow 20% larger for 7 seconds, gaining 35% Bullet Resist, 35% resistance to spirit damage and 30% melee damage, and slowing enemies within 14 metres by 24%. The cooldown is 37 seconds. It also adds 25% base health and 15% Weapon Damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns you into a tank for the length of a big fight, and the slow makes it hard for enemies to escape or reach your allies.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it when you step into the middle of a team fight. Being bigger also makes you easier to hit, so use it only when the defence is worth it.

name: Compress Cooldown
text: Imbue an ability to reduce its Cooldown.

effects.text: Imbue an ability to reduce its Cooldown.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 spirit item that costs 1,600 souls. You attach it to one of your abilities, which then has 18% less cooldown. It builds into Superior Cooldown.
beginner.whyItMatters: Your favourite ability can be used more often. Only the ability you attach it to benefits.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pick the ability that does most of your damage or utility. If you cannot decide on one ability, an item that affects all abilities is a better pick.

name: Counterspell
text: Your next parry protects you from the damage and effects of enemy abilities and items. On a successful spell parry heal and gain move speed and Spirit.

effects.text: Your next parry protects you from the damage and effects of enemy abilities and items. On a successful spell parry heal and gain move speed and Spirit.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 vitality item that costs 3,200 souls. Your next well-timed block, with a 0.8 second window, protects you from the damage and effects of an enemy ability or item. A successful block heals you for 150, grants 20 Spirit Power and adds 1.75 metres per second of move speed for 6 seconds. The cooldown is 23 seconds. It also adds 50 health and 5 Spirit Power.
beginner.whyItMatters: A good block can cancel a key enemy ability, such as a stun or a big damage spell, and rewards you for it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it when the enemy has one or two abilities you must avoid, and you can read when they will use them. It takes practice to time.

name: Crippling Headshot
text: Landing a Headshot will reduce their Bullet, Spirit Resist, and Incoming Healing.

effects.text: Landing a Headshot will reduce their Bullet, Spirit Resist, and Incoming Healing.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 weapon item that costs 6,400 souls and is built from Weakening Headshot. Landing a headshot on an enemy lowers their Bullet Resist by 16%, their resistance to spirit damage by 16% and the healing they receive by 35%, for 12 seconds. It also adds 125 health.
beginner.whyItMatters: One accurate shot makes the target weaker against bullets, abilities and healing at the same time. Your whole team benefits while the debuff lasts.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it when you are a skilled aimer and your team wants to burst down a healer or a tough target. If you rarely hit headshots it gives you little.

name: Crushing Fists
text: Your next Heavy Melee attack against an enemy deals increased damage. Your melee damage will restore ammo and apply a stacking bullet resist debuff on enemies. Heavy melee applies 2 stacks. If the target reaches max stacks, they will be stunned.

effects.text: Your next Heavy Melee attack against an enemy deals increased damage. Your melee damage will restore ammo and apply a stacking bullet resist debuff on enemies. Heavy melee applies 2 stacks. If the target reaches max stacks, they will be stunned.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 weapon item that costs 6,400 souls and is built from Melee Charge. Your next heavy melee attack hits for 25% more (5 second cooldown). Separately, your melee damage restores ammo and puts a stacking Bullet Resist reduction on the target. A light melee gives 1 stack, a heavy melee gives 2, and an enemy at 6 stacks is stunned for 0.75 seconds. It adds 22% melee damage and 12% Bullet Resist.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes melee a real part of your damage. The stun at full stacks can set up a kill, and each stack makes the target easier to shoot.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pick it for a hero who weaves heavy melee between shots. It is a niche item, so skip it if you never go for melee attacks.

name: Cultist Sacrifice
text: Target an enemy NPC and consume it for 170% Bonus Souls and grants a powerful long lasting buff.

effects.text: Target an enemy NPC and consume it for 170% Bonus Souls and grants a powerful long lasting buff.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 weapon item with a button, built from Monster Rounds. Target an enemy non-player unit and consume it for 170% bonus souls, plus a strong buff for 160 seconds that adds 10% Weapon Damage, 50 health and 12% ability range. The cooldown is 270 seconds. It also adds 30% weapon damage and 30% Bullet Resist against non-player units.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is an economy item: a single press means more souls and a long power boost. The long cooldown means you only get a handful of uses in a match.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it when you spend a lot of time farming troopers and neutral monsters. Use it on a high value target as soon as it comes off cooldown.

name: Cursed Relic
text: Curses an enemy - interrupting, Silencing, Disarming, and preventing item usage. Removes all non-ultimate buffs. Your own Damage Output is reduced for the duration.

effects.text: Curses an enemy - interrupting, Silencing, Disarming, and preventing item usage. Removes all non-ultimate buffs. Your own Damage Output is reduced for the duration.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 spirit item with a button that costs 6,400 souls. Press it on an enemy within 20 metres to interrupt, silence and disarm them, block their items and remove all their positive effects except ultimates, for 3.25 seconds. While it lasts, your own damage is lowered by 25%. The cooldown is 55 seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It shuts a target down without stunning or rooting them: for 3.25 seconds they are interrupted, silenced and disarmed, cannot use items, and lose their buffs other than ultimates. Disarm only stops their weapon, and they can still move. The cost is a smaller damage output for you during those seconds.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it on the enemy's most dangerous hero just as they start an important move. Do not use it if you need your own damage to finish a kill.

name: Debuff Reducer
text: Reduces the duration of all negative effects applied to you.

effects.text: Reduces the duration of all negative effects applied to you.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 vitality item that costs 1,600 souls. It shortens all negative effects on you by 25% and adds 90 health. It builds into Spellbreaker and Unstoppable.
beginner.whyItMatters: Slows, stuns and silences end sooner, so you spend less time helpless.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it against a team with lots of stuns and slows. It is also the first step toward Unstoppable or Spellbreaker.

name: Decay
text: Inflict damage over time to a target, dealing damage based on their current health. Decay's damage is non-lethal and does not apply item procs.

effects.text: Inflict damage over time to a target, dealing damage based on their current health. Decay's damage is non-lethal and does not apply item procs.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 spirit item with a button that costs 3,200 souls. Press it on a target within 20 metres to deal 1.95% of their current health per second for 12 seconds, and cut the healing they receive by 50%. The damage cannot kill, and it does not trigger item effects. The cooldown is 30 seconds. It also adds 8 Spirit Power and 65 health.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a good way to wear down tough targets and stop them from healing between fights.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it at the start of a fight on a tank or healer. It will not finish a target for you, so combine it with other damage.

name: Disarming Hex
text: Disarms enemy target and reduces their Bullet Resist.

effects.text: Disarms enemy target and reduces their Bullet Resist.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 spirit item with a button, built from Rusted Barrel. Press it on an enemy within 32 metres to stop them using their weapon for 4.25 seconds and lower their Bullet Resist by 13%. The cooldown is 16 seconds. It also adds 75 health and sprint speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: A gun hero who cannot shoot is much less dangerous, and your team deals more damage to them in the meantime.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it on the enemy who relies on their gun most. It does not stop abilities, so against a hero who fights with spells only the Bullet Resist cut helps.

name: Dispel Magic
text: Purge all non-ultimate negative effects currently applied to you. If any effects were removed, heal yourself and gain a move speed bonus. Cannot be used while Stunned or Slept.

effects.text: Purge all non-ultimate negative effects currently applied to you. If any effects were removed, heal yourself and gain a move speed bonus. Cannot be used while Stunned or Slept.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 vitality item with a button that costs 3,200 souls. Press it to remove all negative effects on you except ultimates. If it removes anything you heal for 250 and gain 2 metres per second of move speed for 3 seconds. It cannot be used while stunned or asleep. The cooldown is 45 seconds. It also adds 10% resistance to spirit damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It lets you get out of a slow or a damage-over-time effect and gives you a small heal as a reward.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Hold it for the first slow or silence of a fight. You cannot press it once you are stunned, so use it before that happens.

name: Divine Barrier
text: Remove all non-stun debuffs from the target and provide them with a Barrier and Move Speed. Can be self-cast. Cooldown is reduced by half when cast on someone else.

effects.text: Remove all non-stun debuffs from the target and provide them with a Barrier and Move Speed. Can be self-cast. Cooldown is reduced by half when cast on someone else.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 vitality item with a button, built from Guardian Ward. Press it to remove all negative effects except stuns from a target, then give them a 600 point Barrier and 2.75 metres per second of move speed for 6 seconds. It can target yourself and has a range of 40 metres. The cooldown is 45 seconds, and half of that if you cast it on someone else.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rescues an ally from a lock down and gives them a shield, and the shorter cooldown rewards helping others.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it for a supporting role, or when your team has a carry you want to protect. You can also use it on yourself.

name: Diviner's Kevlar
text: Upon casting an ultimate ability gain a Barrier and temporary Spirit Power.

effects.text: Upon casting an ultimate ability gain a Barrier and temporary Spirit Power.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 vitality item that costs 6,400 souls. When you cast an ultimate you gain a 1,000 point Barrier and 40 Spirit Power for 20 seconds. The cooldown is 40 seconds. It also adds 15% ability duration and 10% ultimate cooldown reduction.
beginner.whyItMatters: Ultimates tend to put you in danger, and this gives you protection and extra power at the same moment.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it for a hero whose ultimate is central to every fight and can be cast often.

name: Duration Extender
text: Imbue an ability to increase its Duration.

effects.text: Imbue an ability to increase its Duration.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 spirit item that costs 1,600 souls. You attach it to one of your abilities, which then lasts 22% longer. It builds into Superior Duration.
beginner.whyItMatters: A longer effect is worth more when the ability is a slow, a shield or a buff.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Attach it to an ability whose length matters, such as a trap or a boost. It is a waste on a short instant hit.

name: Echo Shard
text: Reset the cooldown of the imbued non-ultimate ability. This item's cooldown is increased by the cooldown of the imbued ability.

effects.text: Reset the cooldown of the imbued non-ultimate ability. This item's cooldown is increased by the cooldown of the imbued ability.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 spirit item with a button that costs 6,400 souls. You attach it to a non-ultimate ability. Press the button to reset that ability's cooldown instantly. The item has its own 30 second cooldown, and the ability's cooldown is added on top of that. It also adds 5% Bullet Resist and 5% resistance to spirit damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It lets you cast your best ability twice in a row, which is a big spike of power. The item then has to wait 30 seconds plus the ability's own cooldown.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pick an ability with a long cooldown and a big effect. Press it right after you use the ability.

name: Electric Slippers
text: When sliding, evade bullets, gain fire rate and deal damage to enemies around you. Cooldown is per target.

effects.text: When sliding, evade bullets, gain fire rate and deal damage to enemies around you. Cooldown is per target.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 5 vitality legendary that exists only in Street Brawl, where it can appear among the drafted items. While you slide you dodge 60% of bullets, gain 60% fire rate and deal 100 damage to enemies within 12 metres, and the same enemy can be hit again every 0.3 seconds while you slide. It also adds 2 Stamina and a longer slide.
beginner.whyItMatters: Sliding becomes both a defence and a weapon, so moving around is also fighting.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only used in Street Brawl. Take it if you like to slide through the middle of the enemy team.

name: Enchanter's Emblem
text: While you are above 65% health, gain bonus Spirit and Cooldown Reduction.

effects.text: While you are above 65% health, gain bonus Spirit and Cooldown Reduction.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 vitality item that costs 1,600 souls. While you are above 65% health you gain 15 Spirit Power and 5% ability cooldown reduction. It also adds 18% resistance to spirit damage and 2 extra regeneration out of combat.
beginner.whyItMatters: A little more ability damage and faster cooldowns, with some defence against spirit damage as well.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A good early to middle item for ability heroes who stay healthy in fights.

name: Enduring Speed
text: Reduces the effect of enemy Move Speed penalties.

effects.text: Reduces the effect of enemy Move Speed penalties.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 vitality item that costs 1,600 souls and is built from Sprint Boots. It adds 2 metres per second of move speed, reduces the effect of enemy slows by 25% and adds 2 extra regeneration out of combat. It builds into Juggernaut.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster movement helps you get into and out of fights, and slows are less effective against you.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it if enemies often slow you or if you need to cross the map quickly.

name: Escalating Exposure
text: Dealing spirit damage applies a stacking Spirit Amp that increases your spirit damage to the target.

effects.text: Dealing spirit damage applies a stacking Spirit Amp that increases your spirit damage to the target.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 spirit item that costs 6,400 souls and is built from Mystic Vulnerability. Each time you deal spirit damage to a target you add a stack worth 4.5% extra spirit damage to them, up to 12 stacks, lasting 12 seconds. It also adds 17% resistance to spirit damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: The longer you keep hitting a target with abilities, the more damage they take from you. Each stack adds 4.5%, up to 12 stacks.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it for a hero who can keep casting at the same target for a long fight.

name: Escalating Resilience
text: Grants Bullet Resist when your bullets hit a hero. Each shot can only grant one stack.

effects.text: Grants Bullet Resist when your bullets hit a hero. Each shot can only grant one stack.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 weapon item that costs 3,200 souls and is built from Extended Magazine. It adds 35% magazine size, 75 health and 18% weapon damage, and its passive grants Bullet Resist when your bullets hit a hero.
beginner.whyItMatters: Each shot that hits a hero can give one stack of 2% Bullet Resist, up to a maximum of 30%, lasting 24 seconds. So the longer you keep landing shots, the less bullet damage you take.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it when you are a shooter who spends fights hitting heroes and taking bullets back. It does nothing extra if you rarely hit anyone, so it suits steady aim.

name: Eternal Gift
text: Periodically gain a random permanent stat buff. Reduces your next death's respawn timer.

effects.text: Periodically gain a random permanent stat buff. Reduces your next death's respawn timer.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 5 vitality legendary of the Street Brawl mode; you can only get it when the draft offers it. It hands you a random stat boost that never wears off once every 2 seconds, and it cuts 70% off the wait before your next respawn; that respawn part has a 165 second cooldown.
beginner.whyItMatters: You grow stronger just by staying alive, and dying costs you less time.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only used in Street Brawl. Take it if the draft offers it: the boosts are permanent, so the earlier you have it, the more of them you collect.

name: Ethereal Shift
text: Instantly enter a void state and become Invulnerable for a short duration. Afterwards, gain a variety of temporary buffs:

effects.text: Instantly enter a void state and become Invulnerable for a short duration. Afterwards, gain a variety of temporary buffs:

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 spirit item with a button that costs 6,400 souls. Press it to become invulnerable in a void for 4 seconds. Afterwards you gain 20 Spirit Power, 30% resistance to spirit damage and 3 metres per second of move speed for 5 seconds. The cooldown is 37 seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It can save you from a burst of damage and then makes you stronger once you come back.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Press it when a big attack is about to hit you, or to dodge an enemy ultimate. Plan what you will do when it ends, because the bonuses that follow last only 5 seconds.

name: Express Shot
text: Your next attack will fire twice in quick succession with increased damage and velocity. This attack consumes extra ammo.

effects.text: Your next attack will fire twice in quick succession with increased damage and velocity. This attack consumes extra ammo.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 weapon item that costs 3,200 souls and is built from High-Velocity Rounds. Your next attack fires twice in a quick pair for 125% more Weapon Damage, with faster bullets, and uses extra ammo. The cooldown is 8 seconds. It also adds 60% bullet speed and 8% Weapon Damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a quick burst of damage you can plan for. Both shots need to land, so accuracy decides how much it is worth.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use the shot as an opener or as a finisher on a low health enemy. It suits a hero who can aim reliably and does not mind spending extra ammo.

beginner.whatItIs: A cheap weapon item that adds 30% to your magazine size and 8% to your weapon damage. It has no button to press; the bonus is always on.
beginner.whyItMatters: A bigger magazine means fewer reloads, and the damage bonus applies to every shot. It also adds its 800 souls to your weapon spending, which is what the investment bonus for weapon items is based on.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A sensible early buy for a hero who shoots a lot. It is also a building block: Titanic Magazine and Escalating Resilience are both built from it, and owning it takes its 800 souls off their price.

stats.label: Bonus Spirit Power for Charged Abilities

mods.label: Bonus Spirit Power for Charged Abilities

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 1 spirit item that costs 800 souls. It adds 1 extra charge to abilities that use charges, and 7 Spirit Power for those abilities. It builds into Rapid Recharge.
beginner.whyItMatters: An extra charge means one more use of the ability before you have to wait. It only helps abilities that have charges.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it only if your hero has an ability that holds several charges, or if you plan to build toward Rapid Recharge.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 1 vitality item that costs 800 souls. It adds 210 health and nothing else.
beginner.whyItMatters: Health is the plainest way to survive. It is also a component for Colossus and Fortitude.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A cheap and safe early buy when enemies keep bursting you down, and the first step toward Colossus or Fortitude.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 1 vitality item that costs 800 souls. It adds 2.5 health regeneration all the time and 1.5 more while out of combat. It builds into Healing Booster.
beginner.whyItMatters: It heals you between fights, so you can stay in the lane without going back to base.
beginner.whenToUseIt: An early buy for a hero who gets hurt a lot in lane. The effect is small, so it is mainly useful as a start for Healing Booster.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 1 spirit item that costs 800 souls. It adds 10 Spirit Power and has no button.
beginner.whyItMatters: Spirit Power makes your abilities hit harder. It is also a component for Improved Spirit and Surge of Power, so the 800 souls come back off their prices.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A cheap early buy for a hero that relies on abilities. If you know you want Improved Spirit or Surge of Power later, buy this first.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 1 vitality item that costs 800 souls. It adds 1 Stamina and 12% Stamina recovery. Owning it puts you part of the way to Stamina Mastery, Kinetic Dash or Arcane Surge, because each of those upgrades uses it.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stamina is what you spend on dashes and on jumps in the air, so more of it means more movement.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it for a hero who dashes a lot, or as the first step toward one of the three items that use it.

name: Fleetfoot
text: Removes the Move Speed penalty while shooting. Gain bonus Move Speed and Slow Resistance.

effects.text: Removes the Move Speed penalty while shooting.
Gain bonus Move Speed and Slow Resistance.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 weapon item with a button that costs 1,600 souls. All the time, it removes the move speed penalty you normally get while shooting. Press the button for 3 metres per second of move speed and 40% Slow Resist for 5 seconds. It also adds 6% Weapon Damage and 6% Bullet Resist.
beginner.whyItMatters: Moving at full speed while firing makes you harder to hit and easier to reposition. The button gives a short burst to dive in or run away, and the slow protection keeps you moving.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it when you fight on the move or are often chased. The button comes back every 16 seconds, so use it freely.

name: Focus Lens
text: Target an enemy to Silence them. A portion of all damage dealt during the silence gets applied to the target when the silence wears off.

effects.text: Target an enemy to Silence them. A portion of all damage dealt during the silence gets applied to the target when the silence wears off.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 spirit item with a button, built from Spirit Sap. Press it on an enemy within 25 metres to silence them. A portion (35%) of all the damage dealt to them during the silence is applied again when it ends. It also lowers their resistance to spirit damage by 9% and their Spirit Power by 30 for 12 seconds. The cooldown is 45 seconds. It adds 10% fire rate.
beginner.whyItMatters: It stops a caster from using abilities and sets up a burst of extra damage afterwards.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it on a key target while your team is focusing them. The more damage you deal during the silence, the better.

name: Fortitude
text: After not taking damage for a period, gain health regen. When you are above 75% health, you have bonus Move Speed.

effects.text: After not taking damage for a period, gain health regen. When you are above 75% health, you have bonus Move Speed.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 vitality item that costs 3,200 souls and is built from Extra Health. It adds 375 health. After you go 10 seconds without taking damage you gain up to 2.25% health regeneration, and while above 75% health you get 1.5 metres per second of move speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: A lot of health with healing between fights and speed when you are in good shape.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it as a core defensive item for a hero who gets into fights and then retreats to recover.

name: Frenzy
text: While you are below 50% health, you gain stat bonuses for a duration and existing debuffs on you are reduced.

effects.text: While you are below 50% health, you gain stat bonuses for a duration and existing debuffs on you are reduced.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 weapon item that costs 6,400 souls. It adds 160 health, 15% fire rate and 10% bullet lifesteal. When you drop below 50% health it also gives 40% fire rate, 40% Debuff Resist and extra move speed for 10 seconds, and weakens debuffs already on you.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives you a second wind in the moment you are in the most danger. The bonus can trigger once per 16 seconds, so it helps through a long fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A strong choice for a hero who fights near the front and often ends fights at low health. It offers less value if you usually avoid damage.

name: Frostbite Charm
text: Imbued ability has its Cooldown reduced and gains Spirit Power. When the ability deals damage, freeze the target and apply bonus damage. Cooldown is per target.

effects.text: Imbued ability has its Cooldown reduced and gains Spirit Power. When the ability deals damage, freeze the target and apply bonus damage. Cooldown is per target.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 5 spirit legendary found only in Street Brawl drafts, never in a shop. You attach it to one ability, which gets 50% less cooldown and 70 Spirit Power. When that ability deals damage it freezes the target for 1 second and adds 200 damage. The effect has a cooldown for each target.
beginner.whyItMatters: One ability becomes a fast freezing attack that can be repeated.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only used in Street Brawl. Attach it to an ability that hits often.

name: Fury Trance
text: Grants Fire Rate, Spirit Resistance and Move Speed, and removes the Move Speed penalty while shooting, but Silences you and disables stamina usage and regeneration.

effects.text: Grants Fire Rate, Spirit Resistance and Move Speed, and removes the Move Speed penalty while shooting, but Silences you and disables stamina usage and regeneration.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 vitality item with a button, built from Bullet Lifesteal. Press it for 6.5 seconds of 32% fire rate, 40% resistance to spirit damage and 1 metre per second of move speed, and you can move at full speed while shooting. The cost is that you are silenced and cannot use Stamina. The cooldown is 18 seconds. It also adds 14% bullet lifesteal, 100 health and 6% Weapon Damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: A short, strong window of pure gunplay. The silence means you cannot use abilities during it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it when you can win with bullets alone. Do not use it if you need an ability to finish the fight.

name: Glass Cannon
text: Each hero kill grants permanent Fire Rate (up to a max of 8 times). Death results in the loss of 1 stack.

effects.text: Each hero kill grants permanent Fire Rate (up to a max of 8 times). Death results in the loss of 1 stack.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 weapon item that costs 6,400 souls. It adds 80% Weapon Damage but lowers your maximum health by 13%. Each hero kill adds a permanent 7% fire rate, up to 8 times, and dying removes one stack.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a trade: a lot more damage in return for a more fragile body. The kill stacks reward playing aggressively and staying alive.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it when you are ahead and want to finish games fast. Do not buy it while behind or when the enemy team has several heroes who can burst you.

name: Golden Goose Egg
text: Hatch the egg, gaining souls and permanent buffs. The value of the egg grows the longer you hold onto it. Gain a permanent buff per 80 Souls accrued when hatched.

effects.text: Hatch the egg, gaining souls and permanent buffs. The value of the egg grows the longer you hold onto it. Gain a permanent buff per 80 Souls accrued when hatched.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 1 spirit item that costs 800 souls. It stores souls over time, worth 80 per minute, and you press it to hatch the egg for the souls and permanent buffs. It costs you 15% damage while you carry it.
beginner.whyItMatters: The longer you wait, the more it is worth, and every 80 souls it holds gives a permanent buff when hatched. It also gives +1 m/s sprint speed and +1 out of combat regeneration.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it early if you can afford to play weaker for a while and want a payoff later. Hatch it when you are about to buy a big item.

name: Greater Expansion
text: Increases the range and effect radius of your abilities and items.

effects.text: Increases the range and effect radius of your abilities and items.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 spirit item that costs 3,200 souls and is built from Mystic Expansion. It increases the range and effect size of all your abilities and items by 30%, and adds 10% resistance to spirit damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Wider abilities hit more targets and from further away, so you can stay safe while landing them.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it for a hero whose abilities are area attacks or who wants to stay back.

name: Grit
text: Gain a Barrier for a short duration.

effects.text: Gain a Barrier for a short duration.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 1 vitality item that costs 800 souls. Press it to gain a 200 barrier for 4 seconds, with a 60 second cooldown. It also gives +1 out of combat regeneration.
beginner.whyItMatters: A barrier soaks damage before your health goes down. It is a cheap way to survive a burst. Later you can grow it into Weapon Shielding, Reactive Barrier, Guardian Ward or Spirit Shielding.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Press it when you expect to take damage, such as when you walk into a fight. Keep it for that moment, not for idle use.

name: Guardian Ward
text: Provide the target with a Barrier and temporary Move Speed. Can be self-cast. Cooldown is reduced by half when cast on someone else.

effects.text: Provide the target with a Barrier and temporary Move Speed. Can be self-cast. Cooldown is reduced by half when cast on someone else.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 vitality item with a button, built from Grit. Press it to give a target within 40 metres a 250 point Barrier and 2.75 metres per second of move speed for 6 seconds. You can cast it on yourself. The cooldown is 60 seconds, and half as long if you cast it on someone else. It builds into Divine Barrier.
beginner.whyItMatters: A shield you can give to a teammate in trouble, and teamwork is rewarded with a shorter cooldown.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it when you play next to a teammate who is often under focus, or when you want a shield for yourself.

name: Haunting Shot
text: Your next bullet applies a powerful debuff reducing the enemy's damage output, healing and movement speed. It also deals bonus spirit damage based on the target's current Health. The bullet is larger and penetrates through targets.

effects.text: Your next bullet applies a powerful debuff reducing the enemy's damage output, healing and movement speed. It also deals bonus spirit damage based on the target's current Health. The bullet is larger and penetrates through targets.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 5 weapon legendary that belongs to Street Brawl and is drafted, not bought. Your next bullet is bigger, passes through targets and applies a strong debuff for 4 seconds: 40% less damage, 40% less healing, a move speed cut, and bonus spirit damage equal to 10% of the target's current health. The cooldown is 2.5 seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: A single bullet cripples a target: their damage, healing and speed all drop. The 2.5 second cooldown means you can apply it again and again during a fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only relevant to the Street Brawl mode, where legendaries like this one can be offered by chance as a rare pick from the last draft of round 3 onward (the game data; the wiki only names rounds 4 and 5). Use it there on the enemy who is dealing the most damage.

name: Headhunter
text: Your next headshot against an enemy Hero deals bonus weapon damage, heal you, and briefly grants bonus move speed.

effects.text: Your next headshot against an enemy Hero deals bonus weapon damage, heal you, and briefly grants bonus move speed.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 weapon item that costs 3,200 souls and is built from Headshot Booster. Your next headshot on an enemy hero deals 75 bonus damage, heals you for 4% and gives 1.75 metres per second of move speed for 3 seconds. The cooldown is 8 seconds. It also adds 5% Weapon Damage and 50 health.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes each well aimed shot count for more, and the heal and speed bonus help you survive after the shot.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pick it for a hero who aims at the head well and has a weapon that fires accurately. If your aim is poor, other items give steadier value.

name: Headshot Booster
text: Your next headshot against an enemy Hero deals bonus weapon damage.

effects.text: Your next headshot against an enemy Hero deals bonus weapon damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 1 weapon item that costs 800 souls. Your next headshot on an enemy hero deals 45 bonus weapon damage, then it cools down for 9 seconds. It also gives 30 health.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards good aim and costs little. Headhunter uses it as a part, so buying it early is a first step toward Headhunter.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it early if you are good at landing headshots. Aim for a head at the start of a fight so the bonus lands.

name: Healbane
text: Your spirit damage reduces the enemy's Incoming Healing. If an enemy hero dies under this effect, you receive a large heal.

effects.text: Your spirit damage reduces the enemy's Incoming Healing. If an enemy hero dies under this effect, you receive a large heal.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 vitality item that costs 1,600 souls. Your spirit damage lowers the healing the enemy receives by 35% for 8 seconds. If an enemy hero dies while under this effect, you heal for 275. It also adds 7 Spirit Power.
beginner.whyItMatters: It stops enemy healers and lifesteal from undoing your damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it when the enemy team has a healer or heroes who heal from damage, and you deal spirit damage.

name: Healing Booster
text: Increases the effectiveness of your healing.

effects.text: Increases the effectiveness of your healing.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 vitality item that costs 1,600 souls and is built from Extra Regen. It makes your healing 20% more effective and adds 3 health regeneration and 1 more out of combat. It builds into Healing Tempo.
beginner.whyItMatters: Everything that heals you works a little better, which pays off for heroes with heals and lifesteal.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it when you rely on healing from items or abilities. It adds little if you have no heals.

name: Healing Nova
text: Heal yourself and nearby allies.

effects.text: Heal yourself and nearby allies.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 vitality item with a button, built from Healing Rite. Press it to heal yourself and nearby allies within 18 metres for a total of 325 health over 2 seconds. The cooldown is 60 seconds. It also adds 8 Spirit Power and 5% ability range.
beginner.whyItMatters: A quick team heal in the middle of a fight, which helps everyone who is standing near you.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it when several teammates are hurt and close together. It does little when fighting alone.

name: Healing Rite
text: Grant Regen and Sprint Speed to the target. Gets dispelled if you take damage from enemy players or objectives. Can be self-cast.

effects.text: Grant Regen and Sprint Speed to the target. Gets dispelled if you take damage from enemy players or objectives. Can be self-cast.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 1 vitality item that costs 800 souls. Press it to give you or an ally up to 300 total health regeneration over 20 seconds and +2 m/s sprint speed. The cooldown is 70 seconds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It heals a teammate from up to 30m away. Taking damage from enemy players or objectives ends the effect, so it works best between fights or when you are out of danger.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it after a fight to get back to full health, or on an ally who has retreated. It also builds into Healing Nova and Rescue Beam.

name: Healing Tempo
text: Applying heal to yourself or an ally grants the target bonus fire rate and bonus move speed. Does not apply on innate Regen or passive Bullet/Spirit Lifesteals.

effects.text: Applying heal to yourself or an ally grants the target bonus fire rate and bonus move speed. Does not apply on innate Regen or passive Bullet/Spirit Lifesteals.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 vitality item that costs 6,400 souls and is built from Healing Booster. Whenever you heal yourself or an ally, the target gains 35% fire rate and 1.25 metres per second of move speed for 7 seconds. It also adds 25% healing power, 6 health regeneration, 4 more out of combat and 10% resistance to spirit damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Healing becomes a damage and speed bonus for your team. Passive regeneration and lifesteal do not trigger it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it for a healer who casts heals often on teammates during fights.

name: Heroic Aura
text: Provides Bullet Resist to nearby friendly units. Provides move speed and fire rate to you and nearby allies. Minions get double value.

effects.text: Provides Bullet Resist to nearby friendly units.
Provides move speed and fire rate to you and nearby allies. Minions get double value.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 weapon item with a button. All the time, you and allies within 35 metres get 17% Bullet Resist. Press the button for 7 seconds to give you and nearby allies 26% fire rate and 2.25 metres per second of move speed. The cooldown is 22 seconds. It also adds speed when you sprint.
beginner.whyItMatters: It helps a whole group rather than only you, so it is worth more the more allies are standing with you.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it when your team likes to fight together or push as a group, and use the button at the start of a fight. It is a weaker pick if you usually play alone.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 1 weapon item that costs 800 souls. It makes your bullets travel 60% faster and adds 8% Weapon Damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster bullets reach the target sooner, so they are easier to land on enemies who are moving. Four later upgrades use it as a part: Sharpshooter, Opening Rounds, Armor Piercer and Express Shot.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A cheap early buy if you want to build toward any of those four items. It helps most on heroes whose bullets are slow to arrive.

name: Hollow Point
text: When you are above 65% health, deal additional Weapon Damage and your bullets reduce enemy Bullet Resist.

effects.text: When you are above 65% health, deal additional Weapon Damage and your bullets reduce enemy Bullet Resist.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 weapon item that costs 3,200 souls. While you are above 65% health you deal 35% more Weapon Damage, and your bullets reduce the target's Bullet Resist by 10% for 8 seconds. It also adds 125 health and 4.5 extra regeneration out of combat.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards staying healthy, so it is strongest at the start of a fight or when you have help to heal. The Bullet Resist reduction also helps your teammates.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pick it for a hero who stays at range or has a way to avoid damage. It is a poor choice for a hero who spends most of the fight at low health.

name: Hunter's Aura
text: Reduces nearby enemies' Bullet Resist and Fire Rate. If there is only one enemy hero nearby, this effect is doubled.

effects.text: Reduces nearby enemies' Bullet Resist and Fire Rate. If there is only one enemy hero nearby, this effect is doubled.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 weapon item that costs 3,200 souls. Enemies within 15 metres have 10% less Bullet Resist and 15% less fire rate. If only one enemy hero is near, the effect doubles. It also adds 100 health and some sprint speed.
beginner.whyItMatters: It works without any button. It is especially strong in one on one fights, because the doubled effect weakens that single enemy a lot.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it for a hero who fights up close or often ends up in duels. It does nothing against enemies who stay far away.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 spirit item that costs 1,600 souls and is built from Extra Spirit. It adds 18 Spirit Power and 1.5 health regeneration while out of combat. It builds into Boundless Spirit.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a plain upgrade for ability damage, and the regeneration helps you recover between fights. Because it uses Extra Spirit as a component, you only pay 800 more if you own that first.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it after Extra Spirit when your hero deals most of its damage with abilities. Keep it in mind as a step toward Boundless Spirit.

name: Indomitable
text: The next Stun, Chain, Immobilize, Sleep, Silence or Fear is automatically cleansed. When this happens, you gain a barrier and all your ability cooldowns get reduced by 20%.

effects.text: The next Stun, Chain, Immobilize, Sleep, Silence or Fear is automatically cleansed. When this happens, you gain a barrier and all your ability cooldowns get reduced by 20%.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 vitality item that costs 6,400 souls and is built from Reactive Barrier. The next stun, chain, immobilise, sleep, silence or fear on you is cancelled. When this happens you gain a 325 point Barrier and your ability cooldowns are reduced by 20%. The cooldown is 55 seconds. It also adds 10% Bullet Resist, 10% resistance to spirit damage and 2 extra regeneration out of combat.
beginner.whyItMatters: It protects you from the first lock down and rewards you for it with shorter cooldowns.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it when you face a team with a lot of stuns and slows. It only works once per 55 seconds, so a team with many stuns can still get through.

name: Infinite Rounds
text: Your Bullets have a chance to become unavoidable, piercing through enemies and ignoring their Bullet Resistance. You have infinite ammo.

effects.text: Your Bullets have a chance to become unavoidable, piercing through enemies and ignoring their Bullet Resistance. You have infinite ammo.

beginner.whatItIs: A Street Brawl legendary, tier 5, that exists only in that mode and comes from the item draft. It gives infinite ammo, +200% bullet velocity and +35% fire rate, and your bullets have a 65% chance to pierce enemies and ignore Bullet Resist.
beginner.whyItMatters: You never reload, and most of your bullets ignore armor, so your damage can stay high for an entire round.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Only in Street Brawl. It suits a hero who relies on the gun, since the item does nothing for abilities.

name: Infuser
text: Gain Spirit Lifesteal and Spirit Power.

effects.text: Gain Spirit Lifesteal and Spirit Power.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 vitality item with a button, built from Spirit Lifesteal. Press it for 7 seconds of 70% spirit lifesteal and 30 Spirit Power. The cooldown is 30 seconds. All the time it also gives 13% spirit lifesteal, 10% resistance to spirit damage, 100 health and 6 Spirit Power.
beginner.whyItMatters: Spirit damage heals you more during the button, which suits long fights with abilities.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use the button when you start casting a lot of abilities in a fight.

name: Inhibitor
text: Your bullets build up to reduce the target's outgoing damage and apply healing reduction.

effects.text: Your bullets build up to reduce the target's outgoing damage and apply healing reduction.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 vitality item that costs 6,400 souls. Your bullets build up a debuff that lowers the target's damage by 30% and the healing they receive by 40% for 5 seconds. It also adds 10% Weapon Damage and 150 health.
beginner.whyItMatters: A target that deals less damage is less of a threat, and it cannot heal back easily.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it when you can focus the enemy's main damage dealer or healer with your gun.

name: Intensifying Magazine
text: Increases Weapon Damage as you continuously fire your weapon.

effects.text: Increases Weapon Damage as you continuously fire your weapon.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 weapon item that costs 1,600 souls. Your Weapon Damage grows while you keep firing, up to 45% more after 2.5 seconds. It also adds 20% to your magazine size.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards a steady stream of bullets. The bonus resets when you stop shooting, so interrupting a fight lowers the damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pick it for a hero with a fast weapon who can hold the trigger down. Avoid it if you often stop to use abilities or hide behind cover.

name: Juggernaut
text: Enemies that shoot you have their Fire Rate slowed.

effects.text: Enemies that shoot you have their Fire Rate slowed.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 vitality item that costs 6,400 souls and is built from Enduring Speed. Enemies who shoot you have their fire rate cut by 40% for 4 seconds. It also adds 50% Slow Resist, 2.5 metres per second of move speed, 25% melee resistance and 8 health regeneration.
beginner.whyItMatters: The more an enemy shoots you, the less damage they do. It is a strong anti-bullet tank item.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it for a hero who tanks at the front, especially against teams whose damage comes from bullets.

name: Kinetic Dash
text: When you Dash-Jump you gain Fire Rate and bonus Ammo until your next reload. Lasts up to 7s.

effects.text: When you Dash-Jump you gain Fire Rate and bonus Ammo until your next reload. Lasts up to 7s.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 2 weapon item that costs 1,600 souls and is built from Extra Stamina. When you dash-jump you gain 25% fire rate and 6 bonus bullets until your next reload, for up to 7 seconds. It also adds 1 Stamina and 12% Stamina recovery.
beginner.whyItMatters: Movement becomes part of your offence: every dash-jump gives you a stronger gun. The extra Stamina means you can dash more often.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it if you move a lot in fights, by dashing and jumping around. If you stand still while shooting, this item gives you very little.

name: Knockdown
text: Apply a Stun after 2s. Stun duration is increased against airborne targets. Increases the target's gravity for the duration of the stun.

effects.text: Apply a Stun after 2s. Stun duration is increased against airborne targets. Increases the target's gravity for the duration of the stun.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 3 spirit item with a button that costs 3,200 souls. Press it on a target within 45 metres. After 2 seconds they are stunned, and the stun lasts longer if they are in the air. It also adds 75 health and 5% ability range.
beginner.whyItMatters: A long range stun lets you set up kills from a distance. The 2 second delay means a clever enemy can move out of the way or deal with it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it on an enemy who is chasing or standing still, then follow with your own damage. Do not rely on it against enemies who move constantly.

name: Leech
text: Reduces the effect of enemy applied healing reduction.

effects.text: Reduces the effect of enemy applied healing reduction.

beginner.whatItIs: A tier 4 vitality item that costs 6,400 souls and is built from two components, Bullet Lifesteal and Spirit Lifesteal. It gives 28% Spirit Lifesteal, 28% Bullet Lifesteal, 180 health, 12% weapon damage and 12 Spirit Power. It also reduces the effect of healing reduction that enemies put on you.
beginner.whyItMatters: It heals you from both bullets and abilities, so it works for a hero that does either. The healing reduction note matters against enemies who try to stop your healing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Buy it late for a fighter who spends most of the game in the middle of fights. It is also a good answer when the enemy is cutting your healing.

name: Lifestrike
text: Your Melee Attack applies Movement Slow and heals you for a percentage of the Melee Damage dealt plus a fixed amount. This heal is 40% effective vs non-heroes. Cooldown is 1.5x as long for Light Melee hits.
